question: Why is the normal force smaller than the weight on this incline?
reference: The normal force only balances the part of gravity that pushes into the slope. For a frictionless incline at angle θ, N = mg cos θ, which is less than mg for any angle above 0°. With m = 5 kg and θ = 30°, N ≈ 42.4 N while mg ≈ 49 N.
key_facts: N ≈ 42.4 N for m = 5 kg and θ = 30°
The component of the weight along the slope is mg sin θ
known_wrong: The normal force equals mg on any surface
The normal force is larger than the weight on an incline
